Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

SVE INTERNATIONAL / CORPORATE INFORMATION

Frequently Asked Questions

Practical answers about SVE International, advisory engagements, jurisdictions and publications.

Last reviewed: 9 November 2026 · Website content v0.1

What does SVE International do?

SVE International focuses on strategic and corporate advisory work, including cross-border planning, enterprise transformation, corporate governance, commercial risk and transaction readiness. The appropriate scope depends on the client's objectives and the agreed engagement.

Which organisations does SVE work with?

Enquiries may come from business owners, boards, management teams, investors, family enterprises and organisations considering cross-border or structural decisions. Acceptance depends on scope, capability, independence and applicable requirements.

Which jurisdictions does SVE cover?

SVE works on cross-border matters and evaluates jurisdiction-specific requirements case by case. A location appearing on the website does not imply that SVE holds a professional licence, maintains an office or can provide every regulated service there.

How do I start an enquiry?

Use the Contact Us page and provide a concise description of your organisation, objectives, relevant jurisdictions and preferred contact details. Avoid sending highly confidential documents before the appropriate confidentiality and engagement arrangements are agreed.

Is an initial enquiry a formal engagement?

No. Sending a message, attending an introductory discussion or receiving general information does not establish a client relationship. Any advisory work requires separate scope confirmation, acceptance and commercial arrangements.

Are consultations complimentary?

Fees and any preliminary screening arrangements are confirmed for the specific enquiry. Do not assume that a consultation, diagnostic assessment or subsequent work is complimentary unless SVE expressly confirms this.

Can SVE provide legal, tax or regulated investment advice?

SVE's strategic advisory services should not be treated as a substitute for advice from appropriately qualified and authorised professionals. Malaysian legal services, where applicable, are provided separately by SK Lai & Partners under its own professional and engagement requirements.

How does SVE work with SK Lai & Partners?

Scam Warning

Protecting clients, partners and the public from impersonation and fraudulent communications.

Last reviewed: 9 November 2026 · Website content v0.1

On this page

  • Warning signs
  • How to verify a communication
  • Payment and banking instructions

Recognising suspicious communications

Fraudsters may misuse the name, branding or identities of legitimate businesses and professionals. Exercise caution if someone claims to represent SVE International or an associated business and asks for urgent payments, confidential documents, account credentials or changes to established payment arrangements.

Warning signs

  • Unsolicited approaches offering guaranteed investment returns, special allocations, jobs or preferential access in exchange for payment.
  • Unexpected requests to change a beneficiary bank account, especially near a transaction deadline.
  • Messages from lookalike email domains, newly created social-media accounts or unfamiliar telephone numbers.
  • Requests for passwords, one-time passcodes, identity documents or remote access to your device without a legitimate verified purpose.
  • Pressure to keep an arrangement secret or bypass established verification and approval procedures.

How to verify a communication

Independently confirm the sender through a contact channel you have already verified. Do not use the telephone number, QR code or link supplied in the suspicious message as your sole method of verification. SVE's general enquiry address is info@sve-int.com. An email bearing a familiar name or logo is not, by itself, proof of authenticity.

Payment and banking instructions

Before acting on new or amended payment instructions, confirm the instruction through an independent, trusted channel and follow your organisation's internal authorisation controls. Do not assume that an earlier genuine email thread cannot be compromised. The legitimacy of any invoice or bank account must be assessed in its actual engagement context.

If you suspect fraud

Stop engaging with the suspicious sender; preserve the messages, URLs, payment details and timestamps; contact your bank promptly if money or account details may be at risk; and report suspected criminal activity to the competent authorities. You may also notify SVE at info@sve-int.com so that the allegation can be reviewed. Do not include passwords or unnecessary sensitive information in your report.

Scope of this warning

This guidance is preventive and does not confirm that any particular communication is fraudulent or genuine. SVE cannot guarantee the security of third-party platforms or reverse unauthorised transactions. Any reported incident will be assessed on the information available.

Eric leads SVE International’s cross-border strategic planning, market-entry and execution-readiness work. His remit spans Singapore, Malaysia, the Johor Singapore Special Economic Zone, Labuan, Hong Kong, China, the Middle East, Timor-Leste and wider Asia.

He supports businesses, investors and strategic partners in moving from opportunity assessment to structured implementation.
